newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Prominent Bosnian Serb politician in suicide bid.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Bosnian Serb politician in suicide bid.

text.p: Former Bosnian Serb vice-president Nikola Koljevic shot himself in the head in a suicide attempt and doctors struggled on Friday to save his life, political sources said.

The sources said Koljevic, a Shakespeare scholar and former Sarajevo University professor, shot himself on Thursday in his office in the Serb republic government's seat at Pale, a mountain village outside Sarajevo.
Koljevic, 60, was taken to a hospital in nearby Sokolac with a head wound.

After initial care, Koljevic was removed from the hospital on Friday for evacuation to Belgrade, capital of neighbouring Serbia, in a helicopter provided by the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia, local doctors and NATO officials told Reuters.
Heavy fog had prevented doctors from flying Koljevic to Belgrade immediately after the shooting.
Sokolac doctor Bratislav Borkovac said earlier in the day that Koljevic was in a deep coma and might not survive. "We are fighting for his life," he said.
Koljevic played a prominent public role in the Serb leadership during the Bosnian war but was sidelined after the signing of the Dayton peace agreement in November 1995.

He belonged to Bosnia's ill-fated collective presidency when war erupted in May 1992, and was a member of the ultra-nationalist Serb Democratic Party led by Radovan Karadzic, now an indicted war criminal.
In his fluent English, Koljevic defended the Serb siege of Sarajevo in interviews with foreign reporters and in talks with diplomats.
He was often assigned the task of conveying the Bosnian Serb position to international relief officials pleading for permission to run aid convoys into Sarajevo and isolated Moslem enclaves.

At the close of the war Koljevic, unlike other hardline Serb officials, chose to cooperate with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, who forced his proteges in Bosnia to accept the Dayton peace agreement.
